meta.source: Coded from the published QP and mark scheme (J560/06, Wednesday 14 June 2023), downloaded from www.ocr.org.uk. Derived metadata only — question numbers, marks, mark-scheme codes and skill tags. No exam question text transcribed.
meta.note: Coded in the same sitting as OCR-JUN23-F-P3. Interleaved crossover: J560/03 q15, q19, q22, q23, q24 and q25 reappear here as q1, q3, q5, q6, q7 and q8, marks matching item for item (1, 6, 5, 5, 4, 4 — 25 of the 100). 36 markers summing to exactly the printed 100.

coding_notes: q1, q3, q5, q6, q7 and q8 are J560/03 q15, q19, q22, q23, q24 and q25 and carry identical skill tags, kinds and mark splits to that file, by design.

q4a ('time halves as speed doubles') tagged inverse_proportion then sketching_functions: the mark scheme's whole requirement is a curve approaching but never touching either axis, which is the shape of an inverse proportion.

q16a and q16b are a compound-growth formula given in the question. (a) reads the annual rate straight off the multiplier, so it is tagged growth_and_decay; (b) substitutes a large index and is tagged substitution alongside it. This follows the OCR-JUN25-H-P4 q16 ruling that reading a percentage off a growth formula stays on growth_and_decay rather than exponential_graphs.
q17 tagged simplifying_indices then solving_quadratic_equations_factorising — the route is r^6 = 3r^2 reduced to r^4 = 3, which is index manipulation before any root is taken.
q12b tagged upper_and_lower_bounds: three quantities each rounded to a different accuracy, and the mark scheme's marks are for selecting the right bound of each.
q13b tagged box_plots, median and interquartile_range — the comparison must cite an average and a measure of spread, and the mark scheme awards a mark for each with a context statement.
q19a and q19b tagged surds_simplifying and surds_expanding_and_rationalising: (a) is a one-mark simplification used as the lemma for (b)'s rationalisation of a two-term denominator.
